newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stks close flat, ignore interest rate drop.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stks close flat, ignore interest rate drop.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed flat in thin trade, ignoring a two percentage point drop in interest rates at Wednesday's auction of Central Bank TEM bills, traders said.

"We'll have to wait for CANTV to come to the market before the bolsa really starts moving again," said Cavelba broker Eduardo Blanco. The Venezuelan government is due to sell its stake in telephone company CANTV on Friday.
The market's 19-share .IBC index closed off 0.02 percent at 6,051.74 as 15.3 million shares traded, worth four billion bolivars ($8.5 million).
Among the day's traded issues, 15 rose, 15 fell and nine closed flat. Among widely-held shares steel company Sivensa lost 2.55 bolivars after nearly two weeks of rises to close at 354.45 bolivars.
Current market leader Electricidad de Caracas finished unchanged at 540.00 bolivars despite a cross trade of over three million shares.
With 50 million shares earmarked for the local bolsa, CANTV is expected to lead the Caracas bourse.
GTE Corp, which already owns about 20.4 percent of CANTV through the VenWorld consortium, said Wednesday it plans to acquire up to $200 million of new shares.
Government officials have said demand for shares in the global offering, which is expected to rise above $1 billion, so far twice outstrips supply.
-- Ana Isabel Martinez, Caracas newsroom, 582 505 2600 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
